messages.author: 18709f130bdf69d6
messages.subject: Installing rstan on a cluster
parts:
When installing rstan on a cluster, how should one go about choosing the number of cores to use for the build (in the line Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = "-j4")? If each node in the cluster has 16 cores, does it make sense to set the value to 16? What if a user wants to run stan across multiple nodes with MPI? Or does it make the most sense to keep the value at 4 in any case, since most people will be running no more than 4 chains in parallel anyway? I would really appreciate any advice on this setting.

Thanks,
John

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Installing rstan on a cluster
parts:
On Sunday, January 18, 2015 at 12:07:23 PM UTC-5, John Palmer wrote:
When installing rstan on a cluster, how should one go about choosing the number of cores to use for the build (in the line Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = "-j4")? If each node in the cluster has 16 cores, does it make sense to set the value to 16? What if a user wants to run stan across multiple nodes with MPI? Or does it make the most sense to keep the value at 4 in any case, since most people will be running no more than 4 chains in parallel anyway? I would really appreciate any advice on this setting.

The numer of cores at build time does not affect the number of cores at run time. And it doesn't take that long to install Stan, so it doesn't really matter whether you do -j4 or -8 or whatever.

I am not aware of any experience with MPI specifically but everyone's cluster is different, so it wouldn't surprise me if someone has done it. What interface(s) to Stan are we considering here? If we are talking RStan, then I would think using parallel::mclapply on one 16 core node would be fine (if you have enough RAM). Stan cannot yet parallelize functions, so the only option is to parallelize chains, and I haven't seen a need for more than 16 chains.

Ben

messages.author: 18709f130bdf69d6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installing rstan on a cluster
parts:
Thanks very much - that is really helpful.

I'm using stan with the R interface, and my thoughts for possible MPI use are not to run more than 16 chains (or even more than 4 probably), but to run multiple models, via parLapply or another function that works with rmpi. Anyway, it sounds like that should not be a problem and it's good to know that I don't need to worry about the initial -j4 setting.

Thanks again,
John

messages.author: 18709f130bdf69d6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installing rstan on a cluster
parts:
I'll let you know how it goes. So far I've just been running parallel chains within each node, using mclapply as well as foreach and doMC, and combining the results with sflist2stanfit, which works beautifully. I've been parallelizing models across nodes manually by submitting multiple jobs at once with "qsub -pe make 4 ..." for each job (we're using Open Grid Scheduler). I've been doing up to 5 models at once this way (20 cores total), and it seems to be working fine.

I will keep you updated and if there is anything I can do to help with stan development or documentation, please let me know. I really like this project.

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installing rstan on a cluster
parts:
Albeit this is off-topic for stan: You may want to consider the doRNG package to make your foreach runs 100% reproducible, i.e. doRNG provides a sane management of your seeds for any "do"-engine.

When simulating from a posterior, I always run with openMP as each draw needs to be processed independently of the other. This works really nice and I am only limited in speed due to fairly slow data passing between R and stan when you simulate a lot of data. This is mostly due to some weird behavior of Rcpp, but if I keep the simulated data small, then runs are really fast.

Best,
Sebastian
